correctness.rationale: Each rounded row belongs to one of four vectors (L,L),(U,L),(L,U),(U,U) with respective independent probabilities a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i. Exact real rank drops below two precisely when all nonzero row vectors occupy one one-dimensional line. If L=0, the three line events (diagonal and two coordinate axes) overlap only at all-zero rows, yielding P(rank2)=1-product(a+b)-product(a+c)-product(a+d)+2product(a). If U=0, complement endpoint probabilities. For L=-U !=0 the four row types occupy two distinct lines so P=1-product(a+d)-product(b+c); for nonzero nonopposite levels three distinct lines yield P=1-product(a+d)-product b-product c. This partitions all L<U, even degenerate p_i,q_i. For p_i=q_i=alpha/N, binomial/exponential limits give (1-exp(-alpha))^2 at zero lower endpoint and 1-exp(-2alpha) at opposite/generic levels, despite equal spacing and per-entry variance. Independently exhaustively enumerated N=2 row pairs with p=q=1/4, yielding exact 15/128, 15/32, 69/128 in the three cases; proof covers arbitrary N by line-event geometry. Dependence boundary: common random bit per row can force identical columns.
